newsitem.title: HONG KONG: No threat to HK's Tung from landslips -- official.
newsitem.headline: No threat to HK's Tung from landslips -- official.

text.p: The Hong Kong government assured legislators on Monday that the home of future leader Tung Chee-hwa was not in danger of being engulfed by landslips.

Government radio quoted Secretary for Works Kwong Hon-sang as saying potentially dangerous slopes near Tung's flat, in a block in a flashy district on Hong Kong island overlooking the famous Victoria harbour, were not a threat to his safety.
If there were landslips, they would only affect the tramline scaling the famous Peak, Kwong told a legislator. He added that maintenance work on the substandard slopes would begin in July.
Tung has opted to make his current flat, where he has lived for years, his official residence from July 1, when he takes over from British governor Chris Patten as leader of Hong Kong.
He decided not to move into the sprawling Government House, Patten's residence, saying it was crowded and Chinese geomancers had ruled it inauspicious.

Years of overbuilding on the hilly slopes of the Peak have made landslides a major hazard on Hong Kong island. In 1972 scores of people were killed when a landslide sent a luxury block crashing down in the Mid-levels area.
Monday was the first day of a week-long final sitting of Hong Kong's elected lawmaking chamber.
The assembly, returned in September 1995, will be scrapped at midnight June 30, to make way for a China-backed interim chamber which was set up last December.
